Sheriff.summary: Night: investigate one player, learn Evil or Not Evil.
Sheriff.rules: Night: may investigate one player. Learn Evil or Not Evil (alignment check, R19).

Tracker.summary: Night: track one player, learn whom they visited.
Tracker.rules: Night: may track one player. Learn whom they visited.

Lookout.summary: Night: watch one player, learn who visited them.
Lookout.rules: Night: may watch one player. Learn who visited them, not counting your own visit.

Seer.summary: Each night: told whether two random players share an alignment; a token lets them pick the pair.
Seer.rules:
Tokens: 1 seer token.
  Night: at the end of every night, you are told two random players other than yourself who were alive when the
  night began (players who die that night count, R10), and whether their alignments (Good/Neutral/Evil) are the
  same (alignment check, R19). Instead, you may spend a token to choose the
  two living players yourself (not including yourself). A chosen pair is a visit to both players; the random
  pair isn't a visit. A role-block stops both.

Fortune Teller.summary: Every night: two labeled numbers, how many players were visited and how many visited someone that night.
Fortune Teller.rules:
Night: at the end of every night, you learn two numbers about that night, each labeled: how many players were
  visited (a player visited several times counts once), and how many players visited anyone (a player who visited
  several players counts once). This needs no action. Self-visits (R6) count in both numbers.
  Example: A holds the Katana, attacks B and also uses their own role's action on C, D visits B, and E protects
  themself. Visited: B, C and E, so 3. Visitors: A, D and E, so 3. Equal numbers don't mean nobody was visited
  twice.

Oracle.summary: Night: guess one player's exact role, learn whether it was right.
Oracle.rules: Night: may guess one player's exact role (Astral Visit). At the end of the night, learn whether you were right.

Eavesdropper.summary: Night: pick a player; reads every PM they send or receive the next Day.
Eavesdropper.rules:
Night: may eavesdrop on one player. Only during the following Day (not the Night you eavesdrop), you read the contents of every private
  message they send or receive, as it is sent. Puppeted messages reach you as the puppet's (you aren't told about
  the puppeting). They aren't told.

Archivist.summary: Once (token): sees one role per other player, unnamed and shuffled; half are real, the rest fakes.
Archivist.rules:
Tokens: 1 archive token.
  Night: may spend the token to consult the archive. At the end of the night, let N be the number of players other
  than you who were alive when the night began (players who died that night count): you are shown N roles, in
  random order and without names, of which floor(0.5 * N) are real and the rest are fake. The real ones are the
  roles of floor(0.5 * N) of those players, chosen at random; a role appears as many times as it was drawn, so
  two drawn Vanilla Villagers show twice. This is an exact-role check (R19).
  Each fake is drawn at random from all the roles in these rules, including roles that are in the game, except
  that the result never shows a unique role (R2) twice.

Surveyor.summary: Token: survey a player; learns one random role among them and their two neighbors.
Surveyor.rules:
Tokens: 3 survey tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to survey one player other than yourself. The group is that player plus their nearest
  neighbor on each side in the circle (R11) among the players alive at the start of the night, skipping yourself
  and never counting anyone twice (so with only one or two other players alive, the group is smaller). You are
  told who was in the group and the exact role of one of them chosen at random, but not whose it is. Players who
  die that night can still be chosen. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Census Taker.summary: Night: count the Good or the Evil players (drawn at random) among a chosen player and two random others.
Census Taker.rules:
Night: may take a census around one player other than yourself (a visit to that player only).
  The program adds two other players drawn at random from everyone alive at the start of the night except you
  (players who die that night can be drawn; if fewer than two others are left, the group is smaller). It also
  draws at random whether to count Good or Evil players. You are told who was in the group, which alignment was
  counted, and how many of the group are of it. It counts true alignment and is not an alignment check (R19):
  the Katana holder, framed players and the Ex-Con count as what they really are, and
  Outsiders (e.g. the Roleplayer and the Ex-Con) count as Good. Neutral players are never
  counted, as either Good or Evil.

Profiler.summary: Token: profile a player, learn three candidate roles for them, one true.
Profiler.rules:
Tokens: 3 profile tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to profile one player other than yourself. You learn three different roles, exactly one
  of which is that player's true role. Of the other two, one is drawn at random from the roles of the other players
  alive at the start of the night (including players who die that night, but not yourself), and the other from the
  roles that no player in the game has. At least one of the three is a Good role and at least one is not Good (Evil
  or Neutral), so a result never settles the player's alignment on its own; which of the two supplies the missing
  side is random. When no role fits a draw, that one is drawn from all roles in these rules instead. The three are
  different and listed in alphabetical order. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Coroner.summary: Token: examine a player who died before tonight, learn their role (not if a Mortician cleaned them).
Coroner.rules:
Tokens: 3 coroner tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to examine one player who died before the night began (not one who left the game, and not
  one who dies tonight). You learn their role, unless a Mortician cleaned them: then you learn only that. This is an
  Astral Visit (R6) and an exact-role check (R19).

Chronicler.summary: Token: marks a player; if they ever die, their role is revealed to everyone (unless a Mortician cleans them).
Chronicler.rules:
Tokens: 2 chronicler tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to mark one player other than yourself. This is a visit. The marked player isn't told.
  The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after you die. If a marked player dies, at any time and of any
  cause, the announcement of their death also reveals their true role to everyone (an exact-role check, R19), and
  says they had been marked by a Chronicler (not by whom). A Mortician's clean beats the mark: a marked player who
  is cleaned has their role and will hidden, and the announcement says they had been marked but the clean hid their
  role. You can't mark a player you already marked. Marking a player another Chronicler already marked spends your
  token but adds nothing.

Auditor.summary: Night: audit a player, learn all their nomination and trial votes from that Day.
Auditor.rules:
Night: may audit one player other than yourself. You learn every vote they cast during the Day just before this
  Night, in order: Yes or No on each nomination and Guilty or Innocent in each trial. If they cast none, you learn
  that. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) shows as a single Guilty or Innocent.

Juror.summary: Night: name two players, learn how often they voted the same way all game.
Juror.rules:
Night: may name two different players other than yourself (dead players allowed; Astral Visit). You learn how many
  times they voted the same way, over every Day so far, counted separately for trial votes (Guilty/Innocent) and
  nomination votes (Yes/No), e.g. "the same way in 3 of 4 trial votes and 5 of 9 nomination votes". Only votes
  both of them cast count, and not votes on the nomination or trial of either of them. A doubled vote (Ballot
  Stuffer) counts once. You learn only the totals, not which votes they agreed on.

Bloodhound.summary: Every night: learns the total attacks three random players have made this game. Token: choose one of the three.
Bloodhound.rules:
Tokens: 2 scent tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, code draws three random players other than you from those alive at the start of
  the night, and you learn their names and one combined count: how many Attacks (R3) the three have made in total
  this game, tonight's included, whether or not the Attacks killed anyone. Each player's Katana attacks, shots,
  alert or trap hits and so on all count; a role-blocked attack never happened, so it doesn't. This needs no action
  and a role-block doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to track one player other than yourself: they take one of the three places that
  night and code draws the other two. A role-block stops the tracking (R9) but not the result.

Scrutineer.summary: Night: learn how many of a player and two random others voted Guilty in each of the Day's trials.
Scrutineer.rules:
Night: may scrutinize one player other than yourself who voted in the Day's trials (Astral Visit). Code adds two
  random other players who voted in those trials (never you), and you learn the three names and, for each trial of
  the Day just before this Night, how many of the three voted Guilty, e.g. "2 in the trial of Erin; 0 in the trial
  of Frank". You don't learn which of them voted which way. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) counts once. If there
  was no trial that Day, you learn that.

Cartographer.summary: Every night: learns the sizes of the night's visit groups (visits linking players either way). Token: learns the names in one player's group.
Cartographer.rules:
Tokens: 2 map tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn the sizes of that night's visit groups. Link two players whenever one
  visited the other that night (R6). Direction is ignored: A visiting B links them exactly as B visiting A
  would. A group is a set of players linked to each other, directly or through other players. Every player alive at
  the start of the night (including players who die that night) is in exactly one group, so a player who visited no
  one and was visited by no one is a group of 1, and a self-visit links no one. You learn only the sizes, largest
  first (e.g. "4, 2, 1, 1, 1"). This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to map one player (Astral Visit; yourself allowed): at the end of the night you also
  learn the names of everyone in that player's group. A role-block stops the map (R9) but not the sizes.
  Your own actions never visit anyone, so they never link you to anyone.

Scout.summary: Every night: learns three players (maybe themselves) who were each in a different visit group.
Scout.rules:
Night: at the end of every night, you learn the names of three players (you may be one of them) who were each in a
  different visit group that night. Groups are as for the Cartographer (visit direction is ignored). The names are
  drawn like this: a random player, then a random player outside the groups already drawn from, and so on, so a big
  group is more likely to come up than a small one. If there were fewer than three groups, you learn one name per
  group and how many groups there were. This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it. You never visit
  anyone.

Insomniac.summary: Token: learns the roles (no names) of up to 3 random players who visited someone that night.
Insomniac.rules:
Tokens: 2 insomniac tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to stay awake. At the end of the night, you learn the roles of up to 3 players who visited
  someone that night (R6; a visit to themselves counts), but not who they are: if more than 3 players visited, 3 of
  them are drawn at random. The roles are listed in alphabetical order, and a role shows twice if two of those
  players have it. If fewer than 3 players visited, you learn all of their roles, and if nobody visited, you learn
  that. Players who visited and then died that night count. Only visits count: an action that isn't a visit (e.g.
  an Astral Visit or a Veteran's alert) doesn't. Staying awake is not a visit. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Accountant.summary: Night: audit one player, learn their total token count.
Accountant.rules:
Night: may audit one player. Learn how many tokens they have in total at the end of the night, after any they
  spent that night and any a Magpie stole (token count, R19). You learn only the total, not what kind of tokens
  they are.
  If their role changed at the end of this night, the role just before the change counts.

Medic.summary: Night: protect a player (Standard Defense; 1 token for Strong, 1 token to protect yourself).
Medic.rules:
Tokens: 2 medic tokens.
  Night: may protect one player other than yourself, giving them Standard Defense. Spend 1 token to give Strong
  Defense instead, and 1 token to protect yourself instead of another player; the two can be combined (so
  protecting yourself costs 1 token with Standard Defense and 2 with Strong).

Trapper.summary: Night: trap a player; the first non-Village visitor on a later night takes a Strong Attack.
Trapper.rules:
Night: may place a trap on one player other than yourself and other than the player your trap is already on, or
  may remove your trap (removing it isn't a visit). You have one trap at a time; a new trap replaces the old one at
  once. Traps last even after you die. A trap is armed from the next night on: the first time a
  non-Village player visits the trapped player on a later night, the trap is used up and that visitor is dealt a
  Strong Attack. If several non-Village players visit that night, one of them, chosen at random, is hit. You learn
  that your trap went off, and nothing else (not who, nor whether it killed).

Kitsune.summary: Night: a fox charm swallows one attack on a player; the Kitsune must later release it, same level and cause.
Kitsune.rules:
Tokens: 1 kitsune token.
  Night: if you hold no swallowed attack, may lay a fox charm on one player other than yourself (on yourself, spend
  the token). The charm acts before any other protection: it swallows one Basic, Standard or Strong Attack on that
  player tonight (chosen at random if there are several; Divine Attacks ignore it), which then has no effect; any
  other attacks on them resolve as usual. You keep the swallowed attack and learn its level and how its kill would
  be announced. While you hold it you can't lay a charm: on a night you choose a target, you release it on that
  player (not yourself), as an Attack of the same level whose kill is announced with the same cause (a released
  Katana attack reads as a Katana death), and a survivor is told it came from that cause's role. You keep the
  attack until you release it. You learn whether your charm swallowed an attack, and whether your release killed.

Vigilante.summary: Night: shoot a player, 1-3 tokens for a Basic, Standard or Strong Attack; learns the role of a player it kills.
Vigilante.rules:
Tokens: 3 vigilante tokens.
  Night: may shoot one player: 1 token for a Basic Attack, 2 for Standard, 3 for Strong. If your shot kills them,
  you also learn their role (exact-role check, R19).

Enforcer.summary: Night: visit a player (a token: two) and attack one who made an Attack tonight; Basic, or Strong for a token.
Enforcer.rules:
Tokens: 3 enforcer tokens.
  Night: may visit one player other than yourself. If they made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or
  not; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), you deal them a Basic Attack. Spend 1 token to also
  visit a second player, and 1 token to make your Attack Strong; the two can be combined. If both players you visit
  made an Attack, one of them, chosen at random, is attacked. Tokens are spent whether or not you attack. You learn
  whether you attacked and whether it killed; with one target you know whom, with two you aren't told which.

Veteran.summary: Can't be role-blocked. Token: go on alert, Standard Defense and a Strong Attack on every visitor.
Veteran.rules:
Tokens: 3 alert tokens.
  You can't be role-blocked.
  Night: may spend a token to go on alert (not a visit, R6, so nothing that reacts to visits counts it). While on
  alert you have Standard Defense and you deal a Strong Attack to every player who visits you that night, whatever
  their faction (a role-blocker who visits you is attacked too), however many there are. Astral Visits aren't
  visits, so they aren't attacked. At the end of the night you learn whether anyone visited you and, if so, how
  many, and whether your attack on each of them succeeded, but nothing about who they were.

Sniper.summary: Day: an anonymous shot with 1-3 tokens (Basic, Standard or Strong Attack), fired after a random 0 to n-1 more speaking turns; everyone hears it.
Sniper.rules:
Tokens: 3 sniper tokens.
  Day: on one of your own speaking turns (once a Day), may take a shot at one player: 1 token for a Basic Attack, 2
  for Standard, 3 for Strong. It is fired after a random delay (R25): everyone is told that someone shot at that
  player, then whether they died; nobody is told who shot. If the target died before then, the shot isn't fired
  and its tokens come back. A Defense from a night effect (e.g. the Medic's) has ended by Day.

Prosecutor.summary: Token: prosecute a player, who goes straight to trial the next Day.
Prosecutor.rules:
Tokens: 2 prosecutor tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to prosecute someone. At the start of the next Day, before anyone speaks, the moderator
  announces that someone is being prosecuted; this counts as a successful nomination and they go to trial. It
  counts toward the Day's three-nomination limit, an execution ends the Day as usual, and it can combine with a
  Clerk's rig. If the trial needs a "nominator", the moderator picks a random player.

Philanthropist.summary: Token: hand a player one token of their own role's kind.
Philanthropist.rules:
Tokens: 2 philanthropy tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to hand another player one token of their own role's kind (e.g. a medic token to a
  Medic; one kind chosen at random if their role has several). They are told a Philanthropist handed them a token.
  If their role has no tokens, they are told they threw it away because they have no use for it, so it doesn't
  count toward their tokens (e.g. for the Accountant). You are not told which happened.

Party Animal.summary: Night: role-block one player. Immune to role-blocks.
Party Animal.rules:
Immune to role-blocks.
  Night: may visit one player, role-blocking them.

Roleplayer.summary: Thinks they are a random Investigative role; gets usually false results.
Roleplayer.rules:
You are told your role is X, chosen at random at the start from Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller,
  Oracle and Accountant.
  You aren't told that you're a Roleplayer. The moderator gives you results that are usually false but plausible.
  Exact-role checks see you as Roleplayer (R19). Your night actions only happen in your imagination: they aren't
  visits, have no effect, and no other role sees them.

Ex-Con.summary: Visits a random player each night without knowing whom; reads Evil to alignment checks.
Ex-Con.rules:
Appears: Evil to alignment checks (R19).
  Night: every night you visit a random player other than yourself, and you aren't told whom. A role-block stops
  the visit (R7).

Grunt.summary: No night action of its own; shares the Katana.

Pharmacist.summary: Night: role-block one player. Immune to role-blocks.
Pharmacist.rules:
Immune to role-blocks.
  Night: may role-block one player.

Ritualist.summary: Token: guess a player's exact role; if right, attack them, if wrong, exposed at dawn.
Ritualist.rules:
Tokens: 2 ritual tokens.
  Night: may guess one player's exact role (Astral Visit), spending 1 token for a Standard Attack or 2 for a
  Divine Attack. If right, the Attack is dealt. If wrong, the moderator publicly announces at the start of the
  next Day that you are a Ritualist. The tokens are spent either way.

Puppeteer.summary: Token: puppet a player and chat in their place for the next Day.
Puppeteer.rules:
Tokens: 1 puppet token.
  Night: may spend a token to puppet any player for the following Day (puppeting yourself changes nothing). That
  Day, they are told they are being puppeted, and they can't chat or see private messages; nobody else is told. You
  chat publicly and privately in their place (including seeing their private messages) and can set their claim,
  which appears in the ledger as theirs; that is all you can do for them. They still nominate, vote and so on as
  normal. It lasts one Day.

Fabricator.summary: Night: frame a player as Evil to alignment checks; a token also forges their will.
Fabricator.rules:
Tokens: 1 fabricator token.
  Night: may visit one non-Yakuza player to frame them (no token needed): that night they appear Evil to
  alignment checks (R19); other results are unchanged. On the same visit, you may spend a token to forge that
  player's last will (not anyone else's): if they die of any cause that night, your forged will replaces theirs.
  Framing and forging together are one visit.

Clerk.summary: Token: rig the next Day so anyone successfully nominated is executed.
Clerk.rules:
Tokens: 1 clerk token.
  Night: may spend a token to rig the next Day's votes. On a rigged Day, anyone successfully nominated is executed.
  The Guilty/Innocent vote still happens; if a majority votes Guilty, the rig is not announced, otherwise it is
  announced publicly.

Smuggler.summary: Token: swap two players for the night, so every action aimed at one lands on the other. Immune to role-blocks.
Smuggler.rules:
Immune to role-blocks.
  Tokens: 2 swap tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to swap two different living players (yourself included) for the night (R23). You visit
  both of them. Both swapped players are told they were swapped, but not with whom.

Ballot Stuffer.summary: Token: their vote counts twice in the next Day's trials.
Ballot Stuffer.rules:
Tokens: 2 ballot tokens.
  Night: may spend a token so that during the following Day your vote counts twice in every Guilty/Innocent trial
  vote. It does not count twice in nomination (Yes/No) votes, which stay one vote each. A trial that Day needs a
  majority of all votes counted, so your extra vote counts whether you vote Guilty or Innocent. The announced
  totals include your extra vote without saying whose it is.

Fixer.summary: Token: one player's trial votes count as the opposite the next Day; nobody is told.
Fixer.rules:
Tokens: 2 fixer tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to fix one player other than yourself. During the following Day, every Guilty/Innocent
  trial vote they cast counts as the opposite (Guilty as Innocent, Innocent as Guilty). Their nomination (Yes/No)
  votes are unchanged. Nobody is told, not even them: their private reminder shows the vote they cast, while the
  totals and anything that reports how they voted (e.g. the Auditor, the Informant, a Jester's revenge on Guilty
  voters) use the vote as counted.

Diviner.summary: Night: pick a player; a Yakuza gets Strong Defense, else learn a role from them and neighbors (60% theirs).
Diviner.rules:
Night: may pick one player. If they are Yakuza, they get Strong Defense for that night. Otherwise, the group is
  that player plus their nearest neighbor on each side in the circle (R11) among the players alive at the start of
  the night, skipping yourself and never counting anyone twice. You are told who was in the group and the exact
  role of one of them (exact-role check, R19), but not whose it is: it is the player you picked with 60% chance,
  otherwise one of the others (20% each, or 40% if there is only one other). Yakuza in the group and players who
  die that night can be drawn too.

Mortician.summary: Token: clean a player; if they die that night, their will is hidden and a Coroner can't read their role.
Mortician.rules:
Tokens: 3 mortician tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to try to clean someone. If they die that night by any cause, they are cleaned: their
  death is revealed publicly with its cause, but their last will shows as "cleaned by mortician". You are
  privately told their role and last will. A Coroner who examines a cleaned player learns nothing, and a
  cleaned player's role stays hidden even if a Chronicler marked them (the announcement says so). The token is
  spent even if they survive.

Wiretap.summary: Passively reads every Day PM between any players.
Wiretap.rules:
You passively read the contents of every private message sent during the Day, between any two players. This is
  not a night action or a visit, so role-blocks don't stop it. Puppeted messages reach you as the puppet's (you
  aren't told about the puppeting). Nobody is told that a Wiretap exists.

Informant.summary: Passively sees how every player voted in each trial.
Informant.rules:
You passively see how every player voted in each Guilty/Innocent trial vote, right after the vote. This is not a
  night action or a visit, so role-blocks don't stop it. Nobody is told that an Informant exists, and the other
  Yakuza aren't told the votes: what you share in the night chat is up to you.

Talent Agent.summary: Token (one a night): learn a random non-Yakuza role in play and one not, or how many living players have a named role.
Talent Agent.rules:
Tokens: 3 talent tokens, at most one a night.
  Night: may spend a token on one of these (not a visit; it targets no player). "In play" means the true role of a
  player alive when the night began (an exact-role check, R19):
  - Scan: learn one random non-Yakuza role that is in play and one random non-Yakuza role from these rules that
    isn't.
  - Count: name any role in these rules and learn how many players have it in play.

Vulture.summary: Wins alone if alive when few enough players remain at dawn. Learns a role for each death, true only half the time.
Vulture.rules:
Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and max(floor(N/4), 2) or fewer
  players are alive, counting yourself, where N is the number of players at the start of the game. The game then
  ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles that never block wins still count, R1).
  Night: none.
  Day: at the start of each Day, you learn a role for each player who died since the previous Day began (during that
  Day or the night after it; not players who left the game): with 50% chance it is their true
  role (exact-role check, R19), otherwise it is a different role drawn at random
  from all the roles in these rules. You aren't told which. This isn't an action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Serial Killer.summary: Night: Strong Attack on one player. Wins alone. Standard Defense.
Serial Killer.rules:
Defense: Standard. Appears: Not Evil to the Sheriff.
  Win: only alone (not even with another Serial Killer).
  Night: may deal a Strong Attack to one player.

Arsonist.summary: Night: douse a player (only non-Good ones are told), or ignite all doused players with a Strong Attack. Wins alone.
Arsonist.rules:
Defense: Standard. Appears: Not Evil to the Sheriff.
  Win: only alone (not even with another Arsonist).
  Night: may douse one player, or ignite (Astral Visit), dealing a Strong Attack to every doused player. A doused
  player who isn't Good (Yakuza or Neutral) is told at the end of the night that an Arsonist doused them; Good
  players are never told. Igniting uses up every douse: players who survive it are no longer doused.

Bounty Hunter.summary: Has 3 random targets and one Strong Attack; wins and leaves once 2 targets die by its attack or by a hanging it voted Guilty in.
Bounty Hunter.rules:
Tokens: 1 attack token. Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get 3 random targets: any players except yourself.
  Night: may spend the token to deal a Strong Attack to one player.
  A bounty on a target is claimed if they die by your attack or are hanged during a Day while your vote counted as
  Guilty. If a target dies any other way (or leaves the game), that bounty is lost. Night deaths are simultaneous
  (R10): a target you kill on the night you die still counts.
  Win: iff you claim 2 bounties. If you are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game
  (leaving works as for the Executioner). If you have died, you still win and nothing is revealed.
  Lose: once you can no longer claim 2 bounties; if you are alive, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave
  the game.

Magpie.summary: Night: steal a token from a player; wins and leaves once it has stolen from 3 different players. Basic Defense.
Magpie.rules:
Defense: Basic. Never blocks wins (R1). Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens.
  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told.
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Jester.summary: Wins if hanged; then a Guilty voter dies. Reads Evil to the Sheriff.
Jester.rules:
Defense: Basic. Appears: Evil to the Sheriff.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you are hanged during a Day (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if the game ends with you
  alive.
  Revenge: if you are hanged, the following night a random Guilty voter from your trial who was alive when that
  night began is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted Guilty, nothing happens.

Executioner.summary: Wins if their target is hanged; becomes a Jester if the target dies otherwise.
Executioner.rules:
Defense: Basic. Appears: Evil to the Sheriff.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get a random target: any player except yourself.
  Win: iff your target is hanged during a Day while you are alive (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if
  the game ends with your target alive.
  On winning: the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game. Leaving works exactly like dying (you
  leave the circle for good) except it doesn't count as a death. The following night, a random Guilty voter from
  the trial who was alive when that night began (not you, since you left) is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted
  Guilty, nothing happens.
  If your target dies any other way, or leaves the game, you become a Jester.

Martyr.summary: If you are hanged, your death announcement says you were a Martyr and names every player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial (rules R24).
Martyr.hover: If hanged, reveals this trait and every Guilty voter (not the role).

Armed.summary: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at a living player: a Basic Attack, in addition to your role's own night action (rules R24).
Armed.hover: One hidden-gun shot a game: a Basic Attack at night, besides the role's action.

Cursed.summary: If you die, a random living Good player is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night (rules R24).
Cursed.hover: If they die, a random living Good player is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night.

Avenger.summary: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack killed you is dealt a Divine Attack and dies too (rules R24).
Avenger.hover: If killed at night, every player whose attack killed them dies too (a Divine Attack).
